task.description: Review ELIXIR-DEV's implementation (handoffs/WF03-ISS0279-20260822/step-03-elixir-dev.json) for ISS-0279 against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md's INV-1..INV-8. This change touches NO tenant-data path in the ordinary sense (no API route, no migration, no auth/tenant-scoping logic, no secrets) -- it is a pure dev-tooling/process Mix.Task (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures.ex) that shells out to `gh` and reads local docs/issues/*.yaml, plus two documentation-protocol files. Confirm this scope assessment yourself rather than trusting it: read the actual diff (git diff main...HEAD -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures.ex docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md) and verify none of it touches lib/letflow/ application code, a migration, a tenant-scoped query, or any secret/credential handling. Also specifically check: does the new Mix.Task shell out safely (no unsanitized string interpolation into a shell command that could allow injection via a crafted docs/issues/*.yaml github_issue field or malicious gh output), and does it avoid printing/leaking anything sensitive (e.g. QUEUE_AUTH_TOKEN, other repo secrets) in its report output. Complete this handoff: status PASS or FAIL, result.summary stating the scope confirmation and invariant-by-invariant applicability (most will be N/A -- say so explicitly, don't just skip them), result.issues, next_action ('Route to REVIEWER' on PASS). Claim by setting status to IN_PROGRESS only.
acceptance_criteria: Diff independently confirmed to touch no lib/letflow/ application code, no migration, no tenant-scoped path
Command-injection / unsanitized-shell-interpolation risk in the new Mix.Task explicitly checked (it shells out to gh with issue numbers/paths derived from repo files)
No sensitive value (tokens/secrets) printed by the new tool's report output
INV-1..INV-8 addressed individually (PASS/N/A per invariant, not blanket-skipped)

result.summary: Scope confirmed independently via `git diff main...HEAD -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures.ex docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md` plus `git diff main...HEAD --name-only -- lib/letflow/` (only hit: lib/letflow/design/iss0279-issue-closure-audit.md, a design doc, not application code). No lib/letflow/ runtime code, no priv/repo/migrations/*.exs, no API route, no tenant-scoped query, no secret-resolution code touched. INV-1 (tenant data isolation): N/A -- no Ecto schema, migration, or tenant-scoped table touched. INV-2 (server-side field authorisation): N/A -- no API response type. INV-3 (sandboxing): N/A -- S5 not started, and this isn't tenant-script execution anyway. INV-4 (secrets by reference only): APPLIES (live) -- verified PASS. The task reads only public docs/issues/*.yaml fields and calls `gh issue view --json number,state,comments,closedByPullRequestsReferences`; no System.get_env, no token/secret literal, no config read anywhere in the file (grep for password|secret|token patterns: no hits beyond doc prose describing QUEUE_AUTH_TOKEN in ISSUE_QUEUE.md, which is pre-existing reference text, not a new secret-handling code path). Error/report output (print_new/print_grandfathered/print_fetch_errors) only echoes issue numbers, file paths, and gh's own stdout/stderr text -- no secret ever enters that data. INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability): N/A -- no lookup-by-ID endpoint. INV-6 (new data-access paths prove scoping): N/A -- not a tenant data-access path; this handoff itself is the required proof-of-scope statement. INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation): N/A -- no SQL, no Ecto.Adapters.SQL.query/Repo.query anywhere in the diff. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): APPLIES -- verified PASS. fetch_issue/1 wraps System.cmd and Jason.decode in a case that returns {:ok, _} | {:error, _} for every branch (non-zero exit, decode failure, and success all handled); audit_one/1 pattern-matches on that tagged tuple exhaustively (:ok and :error cases both present) rather than asserting {:ok, x} =. No bare `{:ok, _} = external_call()` pattern found (confirmed via read of the full 334-line file; the grep heuristic in INV-8 finds nothing in this file). Command-injection check (acceptance criterion): System.cmd("gh", args, stderr_to_stdout: true) passes args as a literal list of strings (issue number coerced via Integer.to_string/1 after String.to_integer/1 parsing, plus fixed literal flags) -- System.cmd does not invoke a shell, so there is no interpolation-into-shell-string vector regardless of what a crafted docs/issues/*.yaml github_issue field or malicious gh JSON output contains; a crafted field can at worst fail to match @github_issue_re (silently skipped) or parse to a large/invalid integer (gh itself would error, caught by the {:error, {:gh_exit, ...}} branch). No secret-leakage vector found in report output (acceptance criterion): confirmed above under INV-4.
